nb_sunnyside_wall.blurb: Sunnyside Wall is a bolted face above Route 7 near Welsford, in southern New Brunswick, and it is one of the crag's six sections. All 15 routes are sport lines. The grades lean toward the middle and upper end: a handful of easy and moderate leads, then a solid block of 5.10 and 5.11 with a few 5.12 and one 5.13 for the strong. Expect steep, enjoyable pitches roughly 60 to 100 feet tall. The wall catches plenty of sun through the day and cools off once the afternoon shade arrives, and the crag as a whole warms early in spring.
nb_sunnyside_wall.approach: A trail climbs steadily uphill from the road to the base of the wall.

nb_gallery_wall_aka_l_shape.blurb: Gallery Wall forms the left arm of the L-Shape cliff at Cochrane Lane, near Welsford. It stands around 200 feet at its tallest, though not every line runs the full height, and the face is mostly a bit less than vertical. Fourteen of the 15 climbs are trad and one is a bolted line. The spread starts around 5.6 and is centred on 5.8 and 5.9, with a few 5.10s and a single 5.11 at the top end. Several routes on the right side end on a ledge, and some are linked into the upper pitches of the neighbouring Joe's Garage.

nb_the_alley.blurb: The Alley is a quiet trad wall of good-quality grey granite perched directly above Gallery Wall at Cochrane Lane, near Welsford. Every route begins from a broad, sloping, wooded terrace, so reaching it means topping out a Gallery Wall line first, which keeps crowds away and makes it a pleasant place for an afternoon with food and water. The 13 climbs are all trad. Most sit between 5.9 and 5.10, with a couple of easier lines near 5.6 and 5.7 and one hard 5.12 at the top end.

nb_lower_dawn_wall.blurb: Lower Dawn Wall is the base section of the Dawn Walls at Cochrane Lane, near Welsford. It suits climbers after demanding bolted lines, with a few of the area's best sport routes, yet also carries some friendly trad pitches. The right half is steeper while the left half lies back as a slab. Of the 14 climbs, eleven are trad and three are sport. They range from a very easy start through the 5.6 to 5.8 band, then thin out into 5.10 and 5.11 with several 5.12s and one 5.13. A short but scrambly approach leads up past a neighbouring wall.
